thread:
sophia: Hi team — partners due date confirmed for Sept 3. I'm planning to take 6 weeks full-time leave as the secondary caregiver and then 2 weeks flexible (work-from-home) over the following month. What do I need to file and how does this affect benefits, 401k, and equity vesting?

ken: Congrats, sophia! Quick map: 1) File a parental leave request in the HR portal now so managers and payroll can plan. 2) If you want job protection, submit the FMLA/CFRA packet (or local equivalent) — secondary caregivers may be eligible too. 3) For pay, secondary caregivers' company-paid leave is 4 weeks at full pay; anything beyond that can be covered by accrued PTO or state benefits. I'll DM specifics on top-up & exceptions.

sophia: I'm a bit concerned about the 4-week company-paid rule 1 I had hoped for 6 fully paid. Is there any flexibility or short-term exception?

dave: We can sometimes approve additional paid weeks on a case-by-case basis for critical hires or long-tenured staff. If you want to request an exception, ping @people-ops with your tenure and a quick rationale and we'll escalate to comp. Note: PTO can always bridge the gap if you prefer to keep pay steady.

sophia: Thanks. And how does leave affect 401k contributions and equity vesting dates?

lina: Good q. 401k: employee deferrals stop if you're not paid; employer matching follows payroll schedules, so if you have paid company top-up it counts. If you use unpaid leave, you won't have deferrals or matching in that window. Equity: Redwood maintains normal vesting for leaves covered by company-paid parental leave; for unpaid extended leave we have an LOA vesting protection policy — submit LOA and comp will confirm. I'll send the policy link.

ken: Payroll logistics: to make sure company-paid leave and any top-up hit expected paychecks, submit leave request + STD/state claim confirmation (if applying) at least 7 business days before the payroll processing date. Our payroll runs semi-monthly: 15th and last calendar day. Missing the window might delay the first payment.

sophia: I'm also curious about splitting leave across parents. Can Redwood split the company-paid time so my partner and I each take a portion?

dave: Yes, you can split company-paid parental weeks between two Redwood employees or between a Redwood employee and an eligible partner under the company policy. When splitting, both employees must submit leave requests and indicate shared leave; we coordinate the schedule so payments and benefits remain aligned.

sophia: What about surrogate/intended parent situations — any special docs?

lina: For surrogacy/gestational carriers we require the legal intent/parentage documentation (court order or agency contract) plus the placement/pick-up confirmation. The HR packet has a "surrogacy" checkbox that triggers the right form set. We'll help you DM those forms.

ken: Ops coverage: sophia, please add a 1-page handoff covering weekly rituals, critical alerts, and a 3-day overlap window for the contractor onboarding. Example snippet you can paste into the runbook:

```
handoff:
  priorities: daily-queue, model-training-jobs, releases
  alerts: pagerduty-team-data -> oncall-engineer
  overlap: 3 days for pairing and knowledge transfer
  docs: link-to-runbook, link-to-deploy-playbook
```

sophia: Uploaded the runbook and set the requested 3-day overlap. I've marked myself as secondary caregiver in the portal.

hr-bot: AUTOMATED: "Parental leave request received for sophia (thread 1745689012). Please upload supporting docs: partner's due date confirmation or legal parentage docs, STD/state claim confirmation if applicable, and dependent enrollment after birth."

payroll-bot: AUTOMATED: "Reminder: payroll cutoff windows are 7 business days before the 15th and 7 business days before month-end. To guarantee leave pay on the next cycle, submit documents by those deadlines."

ken: One more note on intermittent leave: if you want to use leave as periodic reduced hours after return (e.g., 2 days/week for a month), you must indicate that on the FMLA form and coordinate with your manager to align scheduling.

sophia: Great — thanks everyone. I'll submit the STD claim once we have an official due-date form from the clinic and follow up on the exception request for extra paid weeks. Appreciate the help :heart:
